## Question

Ammonia decomposition on Ru had become interesting as a route to hydrogen for fuel cells, but the literature disagreed on which step controls the rate (N2 desorption or N-H bond cleavage), on the most abundant reaction intermediate (MARI: N\*, H\*, NH\* or empty sites, depending on the study), and on how high the N\* coverage can go. Several DFT studies reported strong repulsion between adsorbed N atoms on Ru, yet earlier kinetic models ignored it and some predicted N\* coverages near one monolayer. The paper asks whether adding DFT-estimated N-N lateral interactions to a microkinetic model changes the rate determining step (RDS) and the MARI ([Mhadeshwar et al. 2004](/papers/mhadeshwar2004/)).

## Approach

Periodic slab DFT (DACAPO, PW91, Vanderbilt ultrasoft pseudopotentials, 350 eV cutoff, 18 Chadi-Cohen k-points) was run on 2x2 cells of a three-layer, fully relaxed Ru(0001) slab with N in the hcp hollow at coverages of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 ML, and with H co-adsorbed next to 0.25 ML N. Heats of chemisorption of H and NHx were also computed. These results fed a twelve-step (six reversible pairs) mean-field microkinetic model whose activation energies come from the unity bond index-quadratic exponential potential (UBI-QEP) method, with experimental zero-coverage heats of chemisorption for N and H, temperature-dependent heats from statistical mechanics, and thermodynamic consistency at the free energy level. Only the pre-exponential factors were fit, to atmospheric fixed bed NH3 decomposition data. Four parameter sets were compared against these data and against UHV N2 TPD data: set A (with N-N interactions), set A' (set A with interactions switched off), set B (no interactions, pre-exponentials refit), and a literature mechanism for Cs-promoted Ru (set H). The RDS was identified by a sensitivity analysis that perturbs forward and reverse pre-exponentials together, so equilibrium constants stay fixed.

## Key findings

- DFT gave a linear N heat of chemisorption, Q<sub>N</sub> = 128.2 - 33.3 θ<sub>N</sub> kcal/mol, so the N-N repulsion is about 33 kcal/mol/ML, close to earlier values of 36.3 and 33.9 kcal/mol/ML. The Ru-N bond length was 1.99 Å. The cross N-H interaction at 0.25 ML N was only 6.2 kcal/mol/ML of H.
- The model used Q<sub>N</sub> = 137.0 - 35.0 θ<sub>N</sub> kcal/mol. With this, N2 dissociative adsorption is exothermic at zero coverage (about -48 kcal/mol at 300 K) but becomes endothermic above θ<sub>N</sub> = 0.69, which rationalizes the submonolayer saturation coverages seen experimentally.
- In N2 TPD, only set A reproduced the downward shift of the peak temperature with increasing N coverage: a net shift of 156 °C against 151 °C measured, compared with 27 to 38 °C for sets A', B and H.
- For fixed bed decomposition, sets A, B and H all fit the conversion data fairly well, but set B needed very different pre-exponentials and set A' fit poorly. The authors stress that the parameter set is not unique, and that TPD data are what discriminate between models.
- Without interactions N\* is the MARI at lower temperatures and N2 desorption is the RDS, matching the prevailing view. With interactions H\* is the MARI (followed by N\*), N\* never exceeds about 0.7 ML, and the RDS becomes NH2\* decomposition to NH\* + H\*, with N2 desorption playing only a minor role. NH2\* coverage was only 1e-5 to 1e-8.
- Comparing UBI-QEP energetics with literature DFT showed large terrace versus step differences (for example, N2 dissociation barriers of 44.4 kcal/mol on terraces and 9.2 kcal/mol on steps, against 7.9 kcal/mol from experiment), so the UBI-QEP energetics look more like defect sites. The authors conclude that the RDS and MARI assignments may depend on how the energetics are calculated.

## Significance

This was, by the authors' account, the first microkinetic model of NH3 decomposition on Ru to include N-N adsorbate-adsorbate interactions. It shows that lateral interactions can change the qualitative mechanistic picture (RDS and MARI) even when reactor conversion alone can be fit without them, and that coverage-dependent TPD data provide a sharper test. It is an early example of combining DFT lateral interactions with semi-empirical energetics in a hierarchical, thermodynamically consistent kinetic model.
